paper_metadata.title: Superior high-temperature strength in a low RE containing Mg extrusion alloy with nano-spaced stacking faults

evidence.quote: Traditional high-strength heat-resistant Mg-RE-based wrought alloys often contain a high amount of RE solutes, but their yield strengths at high temperatures, such as 250 ◦C, are still less than 300 MPa.
a low-RE-alloyed Mg – 4Er-2Nd-0.6Zn-0.2Zr (wt.%) alloy with excellent high-temperature strength was fabricated

this alloy characterizes a high proportion of unDRXed grains with a strong basal texture. Therefore, their basal slip is a hard orientation during tension, implying a considerable texture hardening effect formed in unDRXed grains
unDRXed grains contain a high density of residual dislocations, which interacts or tangles with newly activated dislocations during deformation, resulting in dislocation hardening

both Nd and Er solutes have a bigger atomic radius than Mg atom and Er has high solid solubility in Mg, so the stable solutes-hardening is expected to be also responsible for enhanced high strength at elevated temperature
fine DRXed grains contribute to a high yield strength via refinement strengthening according to the Hall-Petch equation
amounts of Mg3RE particles at DRXed grain boundaries may be critical in limiting grain boundary sliding during high-temperature tension
The bimodal microstructure provides substantial refinement strengthening and texture hardening, contributing to the strength of this alloy.

mechanisms.name: dislocation slip suppression by stacking faults

evidence.quote: Nano-spaced SFs can effectively prevent non-basal dislocation slip, stabilize intragranular deformation and resists lattice rotation during high-temperature tension, which is the most essential factor in enhancing high-temperature strength.
profuse Mg3RE particles were dynamically precipitated at DRXed grain boundaries during extrusion, which improves high-temperature strength by suppressing grain boundary migration
a higher density of SFs in unDRXed grains is possibly due to dynamical solute partitioning during extrusion
